data-setup-576-firms: Section 3, p.9: the paper states its dataset and sources in these words, in context.
data-recovery-definition-30-days: Section 3, pp.9-10: the paper defines recovery amount as the bond price 30 days after default and says it follows the literature.
data-recovery-rate-distribution: Section 3.1, p.10: text and Table 2 give mean 48%, median 42%, STD 0.33, max 1.0996, and the bimodal histogram. Description of its own sample.
data-default-year-imbalance: Section 3.1, p.11: 597 defaults 1999-2015 and 1,128 observations 2016-2023, stated for its own sample.
data-feature-categories: Section 3.2, pp.12-14: counts 29, 17, 78 (77 PD plus 1 volatility), 98 (55+43), 34 sum to 256, each stated in the text.
data-preprocessing-zscore-no-pca: Section 3.2, pp.14-15: z-score from training set only, 0/1 mapping, no missing data, no PCA; all stated in one paragraph.
architecture-four-step-pipeline: Section 4, p.15: the four numbered steps are the paper's own architecture description.
architecture-256-features-8-qubits: Section 4.2, p.17: 256 features in eight qubits; the angle-encoding line is the paper's 4-feature illustration of one qubit per feature. Own encoding setup.
architecture-classical-master-layer: Section 4.1, pp.15-16: input and hidden layer of equal size with LeakyReLU, and its stated role as a feature transformation layer.
architecture-pqc-strongly-entangling-par: Section 4.3, pp.17-18: rotation R(alpha,beta,gamma) per qubit, CNOTs of range one, O(3n) parameters and O(3 log2 N) scaling, stated as its own circuit design.
theory-unitarity-limit-classical-inputs: Section 4.4, p.19: the authors state in their own words that the constraints of Eqs. (2) and (4) act on the internal quantum state only, not on classical vectors.
baselines-angle-encoding-auxiliary-layer: Section 4.5, p.19: the angle-encoding baseline has an auxiliary classical layer and O(3Nn) parameters, stated by the paper for its own baseline.
setup-four-fold-cv-100-epochs: Section 5.2, pp.23-24: four folds of 75%/25%, same splits for all models, 100 epochs (100 trees), and LOOCV as a robustness check, all stated.
setup-no-chronological-split: Section 5, footnote 3, p.20: the authors state a strict chronological split leaves too few defaults, so they use four-fold CV. A stated constraint on their own validation design.
setup-simulator-software-hardware: Section 5.1, p.21: PennyLane 0.38.0, default.qubit on i9-13900H CPU, RTX 4050 GPU for classical models, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.4.1, no more than 14 qubits.
setup-hyperparameters-table5: Section 5.1 and Table 5, pp.21-22: Adam, lr 0.001 (FNN, QML), XGBoost lr 0.1 with Newton-Raphson, depth six by grid search, and the statement that backpropagation is not feasible on real hardware.
setup-parameter-matched-baselines: Section 5.2, p.22 and Table 7, p.24: the paper states it matched FNN and angle-encoding capacity to the amplitude model; Table 7 lists 67,857, 67,873 and 65,825.
method-diebold-mariano-assumptions: Section 5.2, pp.23-24: the paper states the independence assumption and the comparison against the standard-normal critical value (printed as 0.05). Own method and assumption.
appendix-b2-amplitude-state-prep-depth-l: Appendix B.2, pp.49-50: the authors state the depth scaling, several hundred operations for 256 dimensions, and that full amplitude encoding remains challenging on NISQ hardware.
supp-definition-uniformly-controlled-rot: Supplement Section 1, p.51: Definitions 1 and 2 are stated by the paper (after Mottonen et al.) for its amplitude-encoding construction.
limit-padding-and-qubit-growth: Section 6.1, p.33: the third limitation, in the authors' words: padding to a power of two, and logarithmic qubit growth (1,024 features need at least 10 qubits).
limit-no-noise-modelling-main-results: Section 6.1, p.33: the second limitation: no explicit noise modelling or mitigation in the main implementation.
limit-classical-master-layer-bottleneck: Section 6.1, p.33: the authors state the classical master layer may reduce speedup benefits and the model inherits interpretability and cost challenges.
limit-economic-significance-7-8-percent: Section 6.1, pp.33-34: the authors state the 7-8% RMSE gain has context-dependent value, quantum cost is higher, and the study is a proof of concept. The 7-8% figure is quoted inside the limit (0.246 to 0.228 is 7.3%).
limit-data-and-code-availability: Declarations, p.35: code on reasonable request and data under a nondisclosure agreement, stated by the authors.
future-work-listed: Section 6.2, pp.34-35: the authors list these directions and state that temporal generalization cannot be assessed directly with the current data.
recovery-rate-simulator-proof-of-concept: Section 6.1 p.32-34 and Appendix B.1 p.47: all QML models are simulator-based and the study is a proof of concept, stated by the authors. The Appendix B hardware run (angle encoding, 100 samples, 32 features, 13 epochs, Rigetti Ankaa-3) is described as preliminary due to resource limits. The new value is accurate and more complete than the stored one.
method-pqkd-overview: Abstract p.2 and Section 1 p.3: the paper's own description of PQKD (16-mode circuit, dictionary convolutions, alternating gradient-based and gradient-free updates). Method description.
def-kd-loss-temperature-lambda: Section 2.1 Eqs. (1)-(2) p.4 and Section 4.4.1 p.17: the objective is defined with lambda in [0,1] and tau^2 scaling; tau = 3 and lambda = 0.5 stated as defaults.
theory-kl-equals-soft-target-cross-entro: Section 2.1 Eq. (3) p.4 and Supplementary S1.1 Eqs. (S3)-(S4) p.27: the identity KL = CE - H is derived from the definition of KL, and H is independent of student parameters. A short derivation is in the paper.
def-dictionary-convolution-photonic-mixi: Section 2.1 Eqs. (7)-(8) p.6 and Section 4.3.3 Eqs. (18)-(19) p.16: the paper defines the dictionary kernel and vec(M) = A z(theta), with A fixed Gaussian entries of variance 1/d and not trained.
def-parameter-count-compression-factor: Section 2.1 Eq. (9) p.6 and Supplementary S3.1 pp.37-38: the paper defines its parameter accounting and the approximate compression factor, ignoring the shared theta term.
setup-fixed-projection-excluded-from-cou: Section 4.6 p.18 and Supplementary p.38: A is excluded from trainable counts, with the caveat that it can add to memory footprint. The paper's own convention and caveat.
setup-photonic-feature-two-marginal-hist: Section 4.3.2 p.16 (steps 1-4): the 16-bit occupancy vector is split into two 8-bit halves, two 256-bin histograms are concatenated into z in R^512. The paper's own feature construction.
setup-teacher-cnn-architecture: Section 4.2 p.15: three conv blocks and GAP classifier as listed; I checked the parameter formula 9c1c2+9c2c3+26c1+c2+11c3+10 and it gives 94,474, 154,826 and 224,394.
setup-partial-compression-45-theta: Section 2.2 p.8 (confirmed on the page image): first two conv layers compressed, about 2.25e5 to 1.50e5 parameters, 45 theta, about 1.5x. The paper's own main-experiment setup.
setup-training-schedule-hyperparameters: Section 4.4.2 p.17 and Section 4.7 p.19: 100 epochs each, batch 64, Adam 1e-3, dropout 0.25, tau 3, lambda 0.5, N=16, d=512, 10 theta updates per epoch, fixed unstated S.
method-spsa-validation-proxy: Section 4.4.3 p.17 and Supplementary S6.3-S6.4 p.50: SPSA with Rademacher perturbation, two evaluations per step, objective is negative validation accuracy or validation distillation loss, 10 steps per epoch.
def-bilevel-alternating-approximation: Section 2.1 Eq. (10) p.7 and Supplementary S6.3 p.50: the bilevel formulation is stated and the loop is said to approximate it by alternating updates.
theory-kernel-lipschitz-in-feature: Section 2.1 Eq. (13) p.7 and Supplementary Eqs. (S49)-(S51) p.41: derived from linearity of M in z and submultiplicativity of operator norms, with the chain of inequalities shown (a small notation slip, S for B, in the last step).
theory-least-squares-mixing-subspace: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Supplementary Note S3.1, Eqs. (S37)-(S42), pp.38-39: m = Az follows from the paper's own generator definition (S38), so the range statement (S39) is setup; with full column rank, which the value carries, the unique least-squares solution and orthogonal projection are standard linear algebra. The only cause of the low grade was that this background fact is stated without derivation, which Rule A says does not make an item low. The reviewer's suggestion was high, proved result; setup is the closer basis.
limit-idealised-best-case-subspace: Supplementary S3.1 p.39-40: the authors say Eq. (S42) is an idealised best case and that the photonic map and finite shots further constrain the attainable set.
setup-fig3-sweep-grid: Section 2.3 Fig. 3 caption p.10: three teacher widths, three compression scopes, dim(theta) in {15,30,45}, R in {4,8,12}, validation accuracy drop against compression factor.
setup-photonic-theta-tiling: Supplementary S5.1 Eqs. (S57)-(S63) pp.44-46: L_tile = N-1 = 15 for N=16, tiles concatenated for longer vectors, and Eq. (S63) zero-pads or truncates.
setup-datasets-and-splits: Section 4.1 pp.14-15: 45,000/5,000 fixed-seed splits for MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, batch 64, no augmentation, and the synthetic 28x28 dataset in the same ratios.
scope-trainable-parameter-compression-on: Supplementary S1.2 p.28: the authors state they focus on trainable-parameter compression and note this can leave inference FLOPs largely unchanged.
limit-photonic-backend-simulated: Section 4.3.1 p.16 and Fig. 1 caption p.5: the authors state the primary backend and that a simulator with the same interface is used when hardware is unavailable; the caption describes an SNSPD measurement. Section 4.7 p.19 says photonic sampling ran on the ORCA simulator.
limit-code-and-data-availability: Methods, p.19: code not public but available to qualified researchers on request; synthetic generator and split indices can be released with the code.
pqkd-simulator-backend: Section 4.7 pp.18-19: photonic sampling was executed via the ORCA simulator backend in CUDA-Q, and the same experiment can be run on the ptseries backend when available. The paper's own setup.

theory_low.theory-unitarity-1-lipschitz: Section 4.4, p.18: a one-line statement of norm preservation by unitaries, with no proof in the paper. The 'learned feature map' claim is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.theory-unitarity-gradient-norm: Section 4.4, pp.18-19: norm identity for U-dagger stated without proof; the no-gradient-explosion and stability consequence is the authors' claim, not tested.
theory_low.theory-spectral-norm-complexity-dominate: Section 4.4, p.18: an argument by analogy to Li et al. and Bartlett et al. bounds. No bound is derived for this model.
theory_low.supp-moettoenen-gate-count: Supplement Section 1, p.53 (checked on the page image): Eq. (11) sum of 2^k = 2^n - 1, Eq. (12) 2^n - 2, total 2^(n+1) - 3, exponents confirmed. But the per-level counts are asserted for the cited Mottonen protocol, not derived here (the CNOT per-level count is not justified), so it is not a proved result in this paper. The drawback statement is the authors' view.
theory_low.theory-finite-shot-feature-noise-bound: Section 2.1 Eq. (12), Section 2.4 Eq. (14), Supplementary S3.3 Eqs. (S45)-(S48) pp.40-41: rests on an assumed Lipschitz property of the feature map, and the sqrt(K/S) rate comes from 'standard multinomial concentration bounds' that are cited, not proved. The main text says 'with high probability' while the supplement bounds an expectation.
theory_low.theory-ema-variance-reduction: Supplementary S6.6 Eqs. (S81)-(S83) p.52: derived under an approximation of independent increments (stated as 'standard approximation'); the ratio 0.0526 is correct arithmetic for beta 0.9, but the measured 0.0406 is one trace, so the claim is an approximation plus a measurement.
